title: Sam's horns and cornet versus trumpet tone
summary: Sam started on cornet, later played trumpet; discussion of the difference in tone and carrying power.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: What kind of a hard did Sam play? I guess he started on cornet too, of course, wasn't he?

He, he started on cornet. He started on CG corn. Then my brother sent him, after he had fell sick, and he got better enough to play, he sent him another, sent him a trumpet from New York, a huge CG corn. That was CG corn.
Did he play trumpet too or did he stick to the cornet all the time?

No, he played trumpet. He played trumpet at the last, on the last session you see. At first he used to use cornet, you see. They said cornet was louder in the trumpets, but the trumpet was further, the sound would go further you know.
Did you notice much difference in the tone when you played the change from one to the other?

Well I, I did. And I still know. The trumpets, the trumpets, with the use now, and at that time you have, you have a further range of blowing, you know. Yeah. The cornet, they're louder. They're much louder, they're close you see, in the close place.
